summary: Phase 1 of a 6-phase production-grade procurement spend cube application. This sprint establishes the complete foundation: project structure, configuration system, canonical pydantic schema, SQLite database setup, reference data files (UNSPSC, FX rates, legal suffixes, abbreviation map, seed mappings), structured logging, synthetic test data generator, and the full ingestion pipeline (date parser, currency converter, cleaner, column mapper, CSV/Excel loader). Validation gate: ingest the 10-row sample messy dataset and produce a clean canonical transactions table with 15+ passing unit tests.

decisions.python_version: Python 3.11+ with pydantic v2 for canonical schema validation
decisions.storage: SQLite for v1 with schema designed to migrate to Postgres — all types chosen accordingly (no SQLite-specific types)
decisions.config: Single config.yaml as source of truth for all thresholds, paths, API settings, FX rate paths. dry_run defaults to true so no LLM calls happen accidentally.
decisions.schema_approach: Pydantic v2 models define canonical schema; SQLAlchemy Core (not ORM) for SQLite table definitions — avoids ORM magic while keeping SQL explicit
decisions.reference_data: All reference data bundled in data/reference/. UNSPSC is a representative ~500-commodity subset covering common procurement categories since the full v24 table is proprietary. FX rates are monthly averages 2023-2025 for AUD/USD/EUR/GBP/SGD/NZD/JPY/CNY.
decisions.raw_data_preservation: All raw source columns stored as JSON in raw_data column so transformations are fully reversible
decisions.date_parsing: Multi-format parser handles DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, DD-Mon-YYYY, M/D/YYYY — uses explicit format chain before dateutil fallback. Always try DD/MM/YYYY before M/D/YYYY for AU data.
decisions.column_mapping: Flexible YAML-driven column mapping in config.yaml maps source schemas to canonical fields. DEFAULT mapping covers the sample dataset format.
decisions.phase_split: This is Phase 1 of 6. Phases 2-6 cover: supplier harmonisation, categorisation, spend cube, dashboards, recommendations. Each is a separate Ralph sprint.

key_files: config.yaml - single source of truth for all settings (to be created in US-002)
src/models/schema.py - canonical pydantic schema (to be created in US-003)
src/models/database.py - SQLite table definitions (to be created in US-004)
data/reference/ - all reference data files (to be created in US-005)
src/utils/logging.py - structured logging (to be created in US-006)
src/ingestion/date_parser.py - multi-format date parsing (to be created in US-007)
src/ingestion/currency_converter.py - FX conversion (to be created in US-008)
src/ingestion/cleaner.py - data cleaning and flag detection (to be created in US-009)
src/ingestion/column_mapper.py - flexible column mapping (to be created in US-010)
src/ingestion/ingest.py - ingestion orchestrator (to be created in US-011)
src/utils/generate_test_data.py - synthetic data generator (to be created in US-012)
data/input/sample.csv - 10-row messy sample dataset (to be created in US-011)
patterns_to_follow: Each module independently runnable via CLI with if __name__ == '__main__' block and argparse
Structured logging via src/utils/logging.py used consistently — JSON format option controlled by config
All transformations idempotent — running twice on same input produces same output
Explicit over clever — no magic, no implicit state, no hidden side effects
Missing columns handled gracefully — canonical schema fields are Optional where source may not supply them
All monetary amounts stored as both original_amount/original_currency AND base_amount/base_currency

userStories.title: Implement currency converter
userStories.description: Implement src/ingestion/currency_converter.py to convert transaction amounts from original currency to base currency using the bundled FX rate table created in US-005.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/ingestion/currency_converter.py — implement CurrencyConverter class
__init__(self, fx_rates_path: str, base_currency: str = 'AUD'): loads data/reference/fx_rates.csv, creates a lookup dict keyed by (from_ccy, to_ccy, year_month_str)

Implement convert(self, amount: Decimal, from_ccy: str, transaction_date: date) -> tuple[Decimal, float | None, str | None] returning (converted_amount, rate_used, warning). Warning is None on success.
If from_ccy == base_currency: return (amount, 1.0, None)
If currency pair not in FX table: return (amount, None, f'UNKNOWN_CURRENCY_PAIR: {from_ccy}/{base_currency}')
If year_month not in table: find nearest available month, apply its rate, set warning = f'RATE_ESTIMATE: used {nearest_month} rate for {year_month}'
Implement convert_dataframe(self, df: pd.DataFrame, amount_col: str, currency_col: str, date_col: str) -> pd.DataFrame: adds columns base_amount (Decimal), fx_rate_used (float), fx_warning (str)
CLI: python src/ingestion/currency_converter.py — converts sample amounts including the DHL USD 8750.00 row, prints conversion table
Verify: convert(Decimal('8750.00'), 'USD', date(2024,2,12)) returns a converted amount between 12000 and 15000 AUD (reasonable range)

Arguments: --rows (default 10000), --suppliers (default 500), --categories (default 50), --messiness (float 0.0-1.0, default 0.3), --duplicate_supplier_rate (default 0.15), --credit_note_rate (default 0.05), --intercompany_rate (default 0.03), --output (default data/input/test_data.csv), --seed (int, default 42)
Output CSV columns: VENDOR_NAME, VENDOR_NUM, INV_NO, INV_DATE, LINE_DESC, AMT, CCY, GL_CODE, COST_CTR, PAY_TERMS, PO_NUM, BUS_UNIT, SITE
Supplier names: generate base names using Faker (company names), then create variants based on duplicate_supplier_rate — same base name with different legal suffixes/abbreviations/capitalisation
Date formats: at messiness=0.0 all dates are YYYY-MM-DD; at messiness=1.0 dates are randomly DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, DD-Mon-YYYY in ~equal proportions
Missing fields: apply missing rates controlled by messiness — at messiness=0.3, ~30% PO_NUM missing, ~20% COST_CTR missing, ~10% PAY_TERMS missing
Credit notes: credit_note_rate fraction of rows have negative AMT and INV_NO starting with 'CN-'
Intercompany rows: intercompany_rate fraction have VENDOR_NAME = 'INTERCOMPANY - [DEPT]'

GL codes: generate from realistic ranges (6420000-6429999 for office, 6510000-6519999 for facilities, 6300000-6309999 for logistics, 6440000-6449999 for IT). At messiness>0.3, some GL codes have leading zeros stripped.
CCY: 90% AUD, 5% USD, 3% EUR, 2% other — with messiness=0 all CCY fields filled, at messiness=0.3 ~10% missing

Run: python src/utils/generate_test_data.py --rows 1000 --seed 42 --output /tmp/test_gen.csv && python -c "import pandas as pd; df=pd.read_csv('/tmp/test_gen.csv'); print(len(df), 'rows,', df.columns.tolist())" — should print '1000 rows' and correct column list

risks: UNSPSC reference data: Full v24 table is proprietary (~50K commodities). Mitigation: build a representative ~500-commodity subset covering all major procurement segments. Sufficient for Phase 3 categorisation demo.

Date format ambiguity DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY: '5/4/2024' could be 5 April or 4 May. Mitigation: explicit format chain always tries DD/MM/YYYY first (Australian convention). Document this assumption in config and README.

pydantic v2 breaking changes from v1: syntax differs significantly. Mitigation: use pydantic v2 throughout — model_config = ConfigDict(...), model_dump() not .dict(), model_validate() not .parse_obj().
Decimal vs float for monetary amounts: Python float loses precision. Mitigation: use Decimal for all monetary fields in schema; convert to float only when writing to SQLite TEXT or doing arithmetic.
